content.heading: Work with us
content.subheading: We are a small team, and we grow slowly. When we hire, we post it here first.

content.body:
Working at Northfold

Everyone at Northfold works on projects from start to finish, from the first site walk to the visit a year after planting. We share the drawing, the site work and the making of tea.

  • Four-day weeks are available for every role.
  • Time and budget each year for training, courses and garden visits.
  • A studio by the river with good light and a yard full of trial plants.

Current roles

We are not hiring at the moment. We are always glad to hear from landscape architects, garden designers and horticulturists in the North East, so do send us a note and some work.

content.text: I like plants that earn their space.

content.heading: Say hello
content.text: Send a short note and a few pieces of work to the studio. We read everything.

content.heading: Get in touch
content.subheading: Tell us a little about your garden, and we will be in touch within a few days.

content.body:
The studio

Northfold, The Joinery, Wharf Lane. We are a few minutes' walk from the river, and there is bike parking in the yard.

The studio is open Monday to Friday, nine until half past five. We are often out on site, so please get in touch before you visit.

What to tell us

  • Where the garden is, and roughly how big.
  • What you would like it to be for.
  • Any timescale or budget you have in mind, even a rough one.

content.caption: The Joinery, Wharf Lane.

content.text: The kettle is usually on.

content.heading: Prefer to talk?
content.text: Call the studio and ask for whoever is in. We will put you through to the right person.

content.heading: How we work
content.subheading: Slowly at the start, so the garden is right at the end.

content.body:
1. Site walk

Two hours on site with everyone who uses the garden. We look at the soil, the light and the drainage, and listen to what you want the place to be for.

2. Survey and concept

A measured survey, then a concept plan with two or three ideas and an honest view of what each would cost.

3. Detailed design

Drawings, a planting plan and specifications good enough to build from, whether you use our contractors or your own.

4. Build and planting

We visit regularly during the build and set out the planting ourselves.

5. The first year

We come back after a year to see what has worked, and adjust. A garden is never finished on the day it is planted.

content.caption: Canes and string: testing a path line on site before anything is drawn.

content.text: We would rather ask a hundred small questions at the start than one big one at the end.

content.heading: Start with a walk
content.text: There is no obligation after a site walk. Some people take our notes and do the work themselves.

content.heading: What we do
content.subheading: Garden design, planting design and landscape architecture, from a first site walk to the first year after planting.

content.body:
Garden design

For private gardens of every size, from a terraced backyard to a few acres. We start with a site walk, then a measured survey and a concept plan, and carry the design through to detailed drawings, planting plans and, if you like, managing the build.

Planting design

For gardens that have good bones but tired planting. Led by Priya Raman, our planting designer, with plants sourced from nurseries close to the studio.

Schools and public spaces

Playgrounds, community gardens and shared courtyards, designed with the people who use them. We are happy to work with parents' associations and small grant budgets.

After care

  • A one-page calendar of what to do and when.
  • A visit after the first year to adjust the planting.
  • Seasonal maintenance visits, if you would like them.

content.caption: The new school grounds in Gateshead, a year on.

content.text: The quiet children have somewhere to be now. That was the thing I most wanted.

content.heading: Not sure which you need?
content.text: Most people are not. A site walk is the easiest way to find out.

content.heading: A small studio for gardens that last
content.subheading: Northfold designs gardens, courtyards and public spaces across the North East, from a workshop by the river.

content.body:
Who we are

Northfold is a landscape architecture and garden design studio of six people. We started in 2019 in two rooms above a bike shop, and now work from a converted joinery workshop on Wharf Lane.

We design private gardens, school grounds, courtyards and the occasional public space. Most of our work is within an hour or two of the studio, because we like to visit often and see how a place changes through the year.

What we care about

  • Gardens that suit the people who use them, not just the drawing.
  • Planting that earns its space in every season.
  • Local materials, reused where we can.
  • Going back after the first year to see what worked.

content.caption: The hillside garden above Riding Mill, three summers after planting.

content.text: They listened more than they talked, and the garden is better for it.

content.heading: How we work
content.subheading: Slowly at the start, so the garden is right at the end.

content.body:
## 1. Site walk

Two hours on site with everyone who uses the garden. We look at the soil, the light and the drainage, and listen to what you want the place to be for.

## 2. Survey and concept

A measured survey, then a concept plan with two or three ideas and an honest view of what each would cost.

## 3. Detailed design

Drawings, a planting plan and specifications good enough to build from, whether you use our contractors or your own.

## 4. Build and planting

We visit regularly during the build and set out the planting ourselves.

## 5. The first year

We come back after a year to see what has worked, and adjust. A garden is never finished on the day it is planted.

content.text: We would rather ask a hundred small questions at the start than one big one at the end.

content.subheading: We are a small team, and we grow slowly. When we hire, we post it here first.

content.body:
## Working at Northfold

Everyone at Northfold works on projects from start to finish, from the first site walk to the visit a year after planting. We share the drawing, the site work and the making of tea.

- Four-day weeks are available for every role.
- Time and budget each year for training, courses and garden visits.
- A studio by the river with good light and a yard full of trial plants.

## Current roles

We are not hiring at the moment. We are always glad to hear from landscape architects, garden designers and horticulturists in the North East, so do send us a note and some work.

content.subheading: Garden design, planting design and landscape architecture, from a first site walk to the first year after planting.

content.body:
## Garden design

For private gardens of every size, from a terraced backyard to a few acres. We start with a site walk, then a measured survey and a concept plan, and carry the design through to detailed drawings, planting plans and, if you like, managing the build.

## Planting design

For gardens that have good bones but tired planting. Led by Priya Raman, our planting designer, with plants sourced from nurseries close to the studio.

## Schools and public spaces

Playgrounds, community gardens and shared courtyards, designed with the people who use them. We are happy to work with parents' associations and small grant budgets.

## After care

- A one-page calendar of what to do and when.
- A visit after the first year to adjust the planting.
- Seasonal maintenance visits, if you would like them.

content.body:
## Who we are

Northfold is a landscape architecture and garden design studio of six people. We started in 2019 in two rooms above a bike shop, and now work from a converted joinery workshop on Wharf Lane.

We design private gardens, school grounds, courtyards and the occasional public space. Most of our work is within an hour or two of the studio, because we like to visit often and see how a place changes through the year.

## What we care about

- Gardens that suit the people who use them, not just the drawing.
- Planting that earns its space in every season.
- Local materials, reused where we can.
- Going back after the first year to see what worked.
